title: Thin Air, Same Lever
endLine: Altitude moves the operating point to where breathing finally buys oxygen.

scenes.tts: Last time, in an adult at rest, breathing harder swung carbon dioxide and p H. It barely moved oxygen content. Now carry that loop up a mountain. The air there is still about twenty one percent oxygen. So why is the climber breathing hard?
scenes.narration: Last time, in an adult at rest, breathing harder swung carbon dioxide and pH. It barely moved oxygen content. Now carry that loop up a mountain. The air there is still about 21 percent oxygen. So why is the climber breathing hard?
scenes.caption: Last time, in an adult at rest, breathing harder swung carbon dioxide and pH. It barely moved oxygen content. Now carry that loop up a mountain. The air there is still about 21 percent oxygen. So why is the climber breathing hard?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and COLOUR MAP without a reset: TEAL = carbon dioxide, ORANGE = oxygen, PURPLE = hydrogen ions, BLUE = the brainstem controller, GREEN = ventilation (the lever), YELLOW = what to look at, RED = removed or stopped, GREY = structure and hedges. THE WORLD, kept all film, at most six things on screen: LEFT 35% a GREY mountain slope in profile with a small GREY climber on it and a GREY barometric dial below reading '760 mmHg'; RIGHT 65% one large alveolus drawn as a tall GAS COLUMN filling about 70% of the frame height, with a GREY ruler beside it ticked 0 to 150 and labelled 'mmHg'. The column is built honestly from the lesson's own arithmetic: a full ORANGE bar labelled 'inspired O2' with a TEAL block subtracted from its top labelled 'CO2 / 0.80', the ORANGE remainder labelled 'alveolar PO2'. At sea level the ORANGE bar reaches 149.7, the TEAL block is 50.0 and the remainder reads 99.7. A GREEN bellows sits at the base of the column; it is the lever. A small GREY tag 'model values' stays bottom right throughout. OPENING MOTION: during the first two sentences the GREEN bellows pumps harder, the TEAL block shrinks clearly and the ORANGE remainder grows by the same amount, while a small ORANGE saturation pip beside the column hardly moves. On 'up a mountain', the climber walks up the slope, the dial winds down from 760 toward 500, and the whole ORANGE bar shortens with it while the TEAL block stays at 50. On the question, large white text across the top: 'Still 21 percent. Why gasp?' Slow ambient motion: drifting ORANGE dots inside the column.

Title 'Thin Air, Same Lever' fades in for two seconds above the gas column while the question text fades out. The climber keeps walking, the dial needle still drifts down, and ORANGE dots drift inside the shortened column.

scenes.tts: What altitude takes is not the fraction. Barometric pressure falls, and the pressure of oxygen in every breath falls with it. The loop is untouched. Its input has dropped.
scenes.narration: What altitude takes is not the fraction. Barometric pressure falls, and the pressure of oxygen in every breath falls with it. The loop is untouched. Its input has dropped.
scenes.caption: What altitude takes is not the fraction. Barometric pressure falls, and the pressure of oxygen in every breath falls with it. The loop is untouched. Its input has dropped.
scenes.visual: On 'not the fraction', a GREY pie beside the climber shows 21 percent ORANGE against the rest in GREY; it stays exactly the same size while the barometric dial winds from 760 down to 500, and a RED cross lands briefly on the pie to say nothing changed there, then both pie and cross fade. On 'pressure of oxygen in every breath', the ORANGE 'inspired O2' bar in the column shrinks from 149.7 to 95.1 on the same GREY ruler, the number beside it counting down. On 'the loop is untouched', the GREEN bellows and the small BLUE controller chip at the top right pulse once at their resting brightness, unchanged. A YELLOW arrow points at the shortened ORANGE bar with the label 'lower input'.

scenes.tts: These are stipulated model values, not a named mountain. Barometric pressure five hundred millimetres of mercury. Subtract water vapour, forty seven. Twenty one percent of the rest is about ninety five.
scenes.narration: These are stipulated model values, not a named mountain. Barometric pressure 500 mmHg. Subtract water vapour, 47. 21 percent of the rest is about 95.
scenes.caption: These are stipulated model values, not a named mountain. Barometric pressure 500 mmHg. Subtract water vapour, 47. 21 percent of the rest is about 95.
scenes.visual: The GREY 'model values' tag brightens on the first sentence. The arithmetic is built on screen as three short steps stacked beside the column, each appearing as the narrator reaches it, in GREY text with the numbers in ORANGE: '500 - 47 = 453', then '0.21 x 453', then '= 95.1 mmHg'. As the last step lands, the ORANGE 'inspired O2' bar settles exactly at 95.1 on the ruler and a YELLOW tick marks that height. The TEAL block is not drawn yet. The climber stands still on the slope; the dial holds at 500.

scenes.tts: At sea level this alveolus sat near one hundred millimetres of mercury. Here inspired oxygen is already down to ninety five. Carbon dioxide is still forty. So where does the alveolus sit?
scenes.narration: At sea level this alveolus sat near 100 mmHg. Here inspired oxygen is already down to 95. Carbon dioxide is still 40. So where does the alveolus sit?
scenes.caption: At sea level this alveolus sat near 100 mmHg. Here inspired oxygen is already down to 95. Carbon dioxide is still 40. So where does the alveolus sit?
scenes.visual: A faint GREY ghost of the sea-level column appears behind the new one with its remainder marked 99.7 and a tag 'sea level'. On 'already down to ninety five', the YELLOW tick at 95.1 pulses. On 'carbon dioxide is still forty', a TEAL chip labelled 'CO2 40' settles at the top of the column, ready to be subtracted, but no block is taken yet and no remainder is shown. Question card in large white text across the top: 'Alveolar oxygen here?' A YELLOW question mark sits on the ruler beside the column with no value chosen.

Predict pause. The question card 'Alveolar oxygen here?' stays, with the YELLOW question mark on the ruler and the TEAL chip waiting at the top of the column. Only slow ambient motion: ORANGE dots drift inside the bar and the barometric dial needle trembles at 500. Nothing is revealed.

scenes.tts: The body gives off about eight carbon dioxides for every ten oxygens it takes up. So forty of carbon dioxide means fifty of oxygen gone: forty over zero point eight. Ninety five minus fifty leaves about forty five, less than half the sea level value.
scenes.narration: The body gives off about 8 carbon dioxides for every 10 oxygens it takes up. So 40 of carbon dioxide means 50 of oxygen gone: 40 over 0.80. 95 minus 50 leaves about 45, less than half the sea level value.
scenes.caption: The body gives off about 8 carbon dioxides for every 10 oxygens it takes up. So 40 of carbon dioxide means 50 of oxygen gone: 40 over 0.80. 95 minus 50 leaves about 45, less than half the sea level value.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. The TEAL chip grows downward into a TEAL block of exactly 50.0 on the ruler, labelled '40 / 0.80 = 50'. What is left of the ORANGE bar below it is relabelled 'alveolar PO2 45.1' and a YELLOW ring marks that height on the ruler. The GREY sea-level ghost column stays beside it so the two remainders, 99.7 and 45.1, can be read against the same ruler; a GREY bracket spans the gap between them labelled 'half'. The YELLOW question mark fades out. On 'eight carbon dioxides for every ten oxygens', a small chip appears beside the TEAL block: '10 O2 in : 8 CO2 out (ratio 0.80)', before the block grows to 50.0 with its '40 / 0.80 = 50' label.

scenes.tts: Low oxygen drives harder breathing, and carbon dioxide washes out, here from forty to thirty. Thirty divided by zero point eight takes only thirty seven point five away. The alveolus rises to about fifty eight.
scenes.narration: Low oxygen drives harder breathing, and carbon dioxide washes out, here from 40 to 30. 30 divided by 0.80 takes only 37.5 away. The alveolus rises to about 58.
scenes.caption: Low oxygen drives harder breathing, and carbon dioxide washes out, here from 40 to 30. 30 divided by 0.80 takes only 37.5 away. The alveolus rises to about 58.
scenes.visual: On 'drives harder breathing', the GREEN bellows at the base of the column pumps faster and brighter, and the climber's chest rises visibly on the slope. TEAL dots stream out of the column, and the TEAL block shrinks from 50.0 to 37.5, its label changing to '30 / 0.80 = 37.5'. The ORANGE remainder grows upward into the space the TEAL block gave up, and its label counts from 45.1 to 57.6 as it rises; the YELLOW ring slides up with it. The ORANGE 'inspired O2' bar does not move: it is still 95.1, and a GREY tag on it reads 'same air'.

scenes.tts: The gain is twelve and a half millimetres of mercury: ten divided by zero point eight. That is alveolar, not arterial, and a model output rather than a measured benefit.
scenes.narration: The gain is 12.5 mmHg: 10 divided by 0.80. That is alveolar, not arterial, and a model output rather than a measured benefit.
scenes.caption: The gain is 12.5 mmHg: 10 divided by 0.80. That is alveolar, not arterial, and a model output rather than a measured benefit.
scenes.visual: A YELLOW bracket spans the climb of the ORANGE remainder from 45.1 to 57.6 on the ruler, labelled '+12.5 mmHg'. Beside it, in GREY, the check is written out: '(40 - 30) / 0.80'. On 'alveolar, not arterial', a GREY label 'alveolar' pins to the column and a GREY blood vessel outline beside it stays empty and unlabelled, with a RED cross over an arterial tag. On 'model output', the GREY 'model values' tag brightens again. The bellows keeps pumping at the faster rate.

scenes.tts: Down here the oxygen sensor has leverage. The ventilatory response to alveolar oxygen is shallow above about sixty, and steepens as it enters roughly fifty to sixty. Forty five and fifty eight sit in that steep region.
scenes.narration: Down here the oxygen sensor has leverage. The ventilatory response to alveolar oxygen is shallow above about 60, and steepens as it enters roughly 50 to 60. 45 and 58 sit in that steep region.
scenes.caption: Down here the oxygen sensor has leverage. The ventilatory response to alveolar oxygen is shallow above about 60, and steepens as it enters roughly 50 to 60. 45 and 58 sit in that steep region.
scenes.visual: Bring back the first film's ORANGE oxygen response curve as a small inset at top left, redrawn in the same colours: ventilation in GREEN up the side, alveolar PO2 in GREY along the bottom from about 40 at left up to 105 at right, the ORANGE band marking 50 to 60, and the GREY tag 'in this sketch'. The YELLOW resting dot from the first film sits at 100 on the shallow part, then slides left along the curve to 45 inside the steep region, where the curve climbs under it. A second YELLOW dot settles at 58. The main gas column stays at right with its 57.6 remainder; the two inset dots are joined to the column's ruler marks by faint GREY leader lines. Nothing on the inset is given a number it does not have.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Altitude does not rebuild the loop. It moves the operating point to where the lever finally buys oxygen. The hemoglobin curve is steep down here too.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Altitude does not rebuild the loop. It moves the operating point to where the lever finally buys oxygen. The hemoglobin curve is steep down here too.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Altitude does not rebuild the loop. It moves the operating point to where the lever finally buys oxygen. The hemoglobin curve is steep down here too.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole world, now quiet and clean: climber and dial at 500 on the left, the gas column with its TEAL block and ORANGE remainder at right, the GREEN bellows at its base, the curve inset still at top left. On 'does not rebuild the loop', the GREEN bellows, the small BLUE controller chip and the GREY sensor at the carotid fork each pulse once, unchanged, and a GREY tag reads 'same loop'. On 'moves the operating point', the YELLOW dot in the inset slides from 100 to 45 once more and stays. On 'the lever finally buys oxygen', the bellows pumps and the ORANGE remainder rises and falls with it, by a visible amount. On the last sentence, a GREY tag appears beside the column: 'oxygen carried: asked below'. No hemoglobin curve is drawn and no content number is shown. Revision: on the last sentence, show no 'asked below' tag; the scene holds on the column.

scenes.tts: The climber does not get the full drive at once. Washing out carbon dioxide raises p H, and that alkalosis inhibits ventilation, centrally and at the carotid body.
scenes.narration: The climber does not get the full drive at once. Washing out carbon dioxide raises pH, and that alkalosis inhibits ventilation, centrally and at the carotid body.
scenes.caption: The climber does not get the full drive at once. Washing out carbon dioxide raises pH, and that alkalosis inhibits ventilation, centrally and at the carotid body.
scenes.visual: The curve inset fades out to keep the frame clear. As TEAL dots continue to leave the column, the PURPLE hydrogen ion dots in the blood band beside it thin out, and a GREY label beside them reads 'pH up'. Two PURPLE-tipped inhibition bars, drawn as in the first film, reach from that thinned PURPLE field to the BLUE controller chip in the medulla and to the GREY sensor at the carotid fork. As each lands, the GREEN bellows eases back from its faster rate to something in between, and a GREY bracket beside the bellows marks the part it is not using, labelled 'held back'. Direction only, no amounts.

scenes.tts: Over days the kidney acts on p H, and the sensors grow more sensitive, so ventilation can climb further. These parts move on different clocks.
scenes.narration: Over days the kidney acts on pH, and the sensors grow more sensitive, so ventilation can climb further. These parts move on different clocks.
scenes.caption: Over days the kidney acts on pH, and the sensors grow more sensitive, so ventilation can climb further. These parts move on different clocks.
scenes.visual: A GREY time strip appears along the bottom of the frame with four unnumbered marks labelled 'seconds', 'hours', 'days', 'longer'; a marker walks along it from 'seconds' to 'days' through the scene. On 'the kidney acts on pH', a small GREY kidney icon joins the world and sends a GREY arrow toward the thinned PURPLE field, which recovers partway; no direction label for any solute is drawn. On 'the sensors grow more sensitive', the GREY carotid sensor and the BLUE controller chip both brighten, and the PURPLE inhibition bars thin. The GREEN bellows picks up again and the ORANGE remainder in the column rises a little further. On the last sentence, the time strip's later marks stay blank and a GREY tag reads 'clocks: asked below'. Revision: on the last sentence, show no 'asked below' tag; the time strip's later marks simply stay blank.

scenes.tts: So nothing in the controller was rebuilt. The mountain carried the same loop, and the same single lever, to the part of its range where a breath counts.
scenes.narration: So nothing in the controller was rebuilt. The mountain carried the same loop, and the same single lever, to the part of its range where a breath counts.
scenes.caption: So nothing in the controller was rebuilt. The mountain carried the same loop, and the same single lever, to the part of its range where a breath counts.
scenes.visual: Final pull-back to the full world. The kidney icon, time strip and brackets fade, leaving climber, dial at 500, gas column, GREEN bellows, BLUE controller chip and GREY carotid sensor: six things. On 'nothing was rebuilt', the controller chip and sensor pulse once at resting brightness. On 'the same single lever', the GREEN bellows pumps slowly and the ORANGE remainder in the column rises and falls with each stroke, the same swing as at sea level but now low on the ruler, between 45 and 58. A YELLOW ring rests on the remainder.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world: the GREEN bellows still pumping slowly, the ORANGE remainder rising and falling with it, ORANGE dots drifting in the column. Large centred white text: 'Altitude moves the operating point to where breathing finally buys oxygen.'
